title: Reduction preserves the integral degree filtration
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] with a nontrivial real-valued multiplicative nonarchimedean absolute value, $n\ge1$, $A=k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring], and $R=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ with the Gauss absolute value. For a finite field extension $E/R$ give $E$ its minimal-polynomial spectral norm $s_G$ [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm]. Write $\widetilde k=\{|a|\le1\}/\{|a|<1\}$ and $\widetilde E=\{s_G\le1\}/\{s_G<1\}$. Under the coefficient-reduction identification $\widetilde R=\widetilde k(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$, view $\widetilde E$ as a finite reduced algebra over this field. Independently give $R$ the total-degree absolute value $|f/g|_t=\exp(\deg f-\deg g)$ for nonzero $f,g$, and let $s_t$ be its spectral norm on $E$. Let $B$ be the integral closure of $A$ in $E$ and $C$ the integral closure of $\widetilde k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ in $\widetilde E$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. Give $\widetilde E$ the spectral norm $ ar s_t$ derived from the total-degree absolute value on $\widetilde k(X_1,\ldots,X_n)$, using the same monic-minimal-polynomial formula. Put $B(
u)=\{z\in B:s_t(z)\le\exp(
u)\}$ and $C(
u)=\{z\in C: ar s_t(z)\le\exp(
u)\}$. For every integer $
u\ge0$, reduction induces an injective $\widetilde k$-linear map $$ rac{B(
u)\cap\{s_G\le1\}}{B(
u)\cap\{s_G<1\}}\ \longrightarrow\ C(
u),\qquad[z]\longmapsto ar z.$$ No completeness, stability, divisibility of the value group, or separability hypothesis is required.

proof.text: Put $F=\widetilde k$ and $D=\widetilde E$. The norm laws of [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] make $E^\circ=\{s_G\le1\}$ a ring and $E^{\circ\circ}=\{s_G<1\}$ its ideal: use submultiplicativity for a product with one factor of norm less than one. By [lem-trf-spectral-reduction-dimension-criterion], $D$ is a nonzero finite reduced algebra over $\widetilde R$. Here $\widetilde R=F(X)$ explicitly: for $f/g\in R$ of Gauss norm at most one divide $f,g$ by a coefficient $c$ of $g$ attaining its maximum absolute value. The normalized denominator has nonzero coefficient reduction; the normalized numerator has integral coefficients. Send the fraction to $\overline{f/c}/\overline{g/c}$. Two presentations give the same fraction by reducing their cross-product equality. Its kernel is precisely the fractions of norm less than one, because $\overline{g/c}\ne0$ and $\overline{f/c}=0$ exactly when all its finitely many coefficients have norm less than one. Conversely lift the finitely many coefficients of any fraction over $F$, lifting zero to zero and nonzero coefficients to units. This proves surjectivity and the claimed identification, including its action on polynomials.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.3.3/3, equation (4), printed pp.216–217 (scan PDF pp.222–223); coefficient reduction and monic-polynomial estimate.

proof.text: Fix $z\in B(\nu)$ with $s_G(z)\le1$. The field $k$ is normal: its fraction field is itself. Iterating [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-ring-normal-domain] shows that $A=k[X_1,\ldots,X_n]$ is normal; the iterated and multivariate polynomial rings agree by grouping each finite monomial by its exponent of the last variable, compatibly with sums and products. Apply [lem-sfb-integral-minpoly-fraction-descent] to $A\subset E$, taking $S=E$ (its fraction field is itself). Since $z$ is integral over $A$, its monic minimal polynomial over $R$ has the form $p(T)=T^r+\sum_{i=1}^r a_iT^{r-i}$ with $a_i\in A$ and $p(z)=0$. The same algebraic minimal polynomial is used for both absolute values: its definition uses only the field extension, not a norm.

source.place: Tags 030A (lemma-polynomial-domain-normal) and 00H7 (lemma-minimal-polynomial-normal-domain), as in BGR p.216.

proof.text: The coefficient formula of [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] gives $\max_i G(a_i)^{1/i}=s_G(z)\le1$, so every coefficient of every $a_i$ is in $k^\circ$. Reducing $p(z)=0$ in the quotient ring of Step 1 gives $\bar p(\bar z)=0$, with $\bar p(T)=T^r+\sum_i\bar a_iT^{r-i}\in F[X][T]$. It is still monic, even if some or all $a_i$ reduce to zero. Thus $\bar z\in C$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. For every nonzero $\bar a_i$, its monomials are a subset of those of $a_i$, so $\deg\bar a_i\le\deg a_i$ and $|\bar a_i|_t\le|a_i|_t$. The same inequality holds if $\bar a_i=0$, since its absolute value is zero. Applying the coefficient formula with the independent total-degree absolute value gives $$U:=\max_i|\bar a_i|_t^{1/i}\le\max_i|a_i|_t^{1/i}=s_t(z)\le\exp(\nu).$$

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.3.3/3, equation (4), printed pp.216–217 (scan PDF pp.222–223); coefficient reduction and monic-polynomial estimate.

proof.text:
First the norm laws of $ ar s_t$ on $D$. By Step 1, $D$ is a nonzero finite-dimensional reduced $F(X)$-algebra, so it is Artinian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], and [lem-sfb-reduced-artinian-residue-product] gives a $D$-algebra, hence $F(X)$-algebra, isomorphism $D\cong\prod_{j\in I}L_j$ with $I$ finite, nonempty because $D
e0$, and each $L_j=D/\mathfrak m_j$ a field spanned by the image of a finite basis of $D$, hence a finite extension of $F(X)$. Corresponding elements have the same annihilating polynomials, hence the same minimal polynomial, so [lem-trf-product-minpoly-spectral-maximum] over $(F(X),|\cdot|_t)$ gives $ ar s_t(x)=\max_j s_j(x_j)$, where $s_j$ is the spectral norm of $L_j$. Each $s_j$ is definite, ultrametric, $F(X)$-homogeneous with $s_j(1)=1$ by [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] and power-multiplicative by [lem-trf-algebraic-spectral-norm-powers]; taking the maximum over the nonempty finite set $I$ coordinatewise, $ ar s_t$ has the same five properties. Put $v= ar s_t( ar z)$. If $v>U$, then $v>0$ and $| ar a_i|_t<v^i$ for every $i$. These laws applied to $ ar z^r=-\sum_i ar a_i ar z^{r-i}$ give $$v^r\le\max_i | ar a_i|_t v^{r-i}<v^r,$$ a contradiction; the term with exponent zero uses $ ar s_t(1)=1$. Hence $ ar s_t( ar z)\le U\le\exp(
u)$, proving $ ar z\in C(
u)$. This argument uses an annihilating monic polynomial, and does not assume that $ ar p$ remains minimal or irreducible.

source.place: Proof of Proposition 5.3.3/3, equation (4), printed pp.216–217 (scan PDF pp.222–223); coefficient reduction and monic-polynomial estimate.

proof.text:
The norm laws of [lem-trf-incomplete-spectral-algebra-norm] show that $B(
u)$ is a $k$-vector space: the total-degree absolute value of each nonzero constant in $k$ is $1$, the ultrametric inequality preserves the bound, and the integral closure is a subring containing $k$ by [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. The same reasoning using the norm laws of $ ar s_t$ proved in Step 4 makes $C(
u)$ an $F$-vector space. Put $L=B(
u)\cap E^\circ$ and $L_0=B(
u)\cap E^{\circ\circ}$. They are $k^\circ$-modules, and $k^{\circ\circ}L\subset L_0$ by $s_G(az)=|a|s_G(z)$. Thus $L/L_0$ is an $F$-vector space. Steps 3–4 show reduction maps $L$ into $C(
u)$; it is additive and respects scalar lifts. Its kernel is exactly $L_0$, by the definition $D=E^\circ/E^{\circ\circ}$. If two elements of $L$ have the same image, their difference therefore belongs to $L_0$. Consequently $[z]\mapsto ar z$ is the asserted injective $F$-linear map.
